Resident proposed tax rate increase rather than override approach; current estimate approximately one dollar eighty-six to one dollar eighty-nine per thousand to generate five million dollars annually
budget_items.quote: mr. bowen recalled a recommendation he made approximately two years ago suggesting that rather than pursuing overrides, the town consider increasing the tax rate by approximately $1.66 per thousand, which he estimated would generate $5,000,000 annually into the town's coffers. in light of the town manager's report indicating a $3,000,000-plus budget shortfall, mr. bowen suggested that approach remains viable, noting that his current estimate has risen to approximately $1.86-$1.89 per thousand.

transfers.description: Regional Dispatch free cash transfer to stabilization and capital account
transfers.outcome: Administrative Board declined to return funds to member communities; retained portion in free cash and transferred balance to district stabilization and capital account due to anticipated assessment increases
transfers.quote: the administrative board declined to return the funds to member communities, opting instead to retain a portion in free cash and transfer the balance to the district's stabilization and capital account, given anticipated assessment increases as grants supporting newer members hudson and sterling expire.

public_comment.speaker: John Bowen
public_comment.topic: Tax rate alternative to override; maximizing investment returns
public_comment.quote: mr. bowen recalled a recommendation he made approximately two years ago suggesting that rather than pursuing overrides, the town consider increasing the tax rate by approximately $1.66 per thousand, which he estimated would generate $5,000,000 annually into the town's coffers. in light of the town manager's report indicating a $3,000,000-plus budget shortfall, mr. bowen suggested that approach remains viable, noting that his current estimate has risen to approximately $1.86-$1.89 per thousand. he also expressed interest in maximizing investment returns on accumulated funds through bartholomew and suggested the approach could reduce reliance on repeated overrides.

topics.resolution: Meeting called to order at 7:00 PM; recording announced
topics.quote: chair caesar nuzzolo called the meeting to order at 7:00 pm and led the pledge of allegiance. chair nuzzolo advised those present that the meeting was being recorded and broadcast live over the lunenburg public access channel, on facebook live, and would be uploaded to the lunenburg access youtube channel following the meeting.

topics.resolution: Citizens Party Caucus March 9; Fire Department fourth shift proposal presentation February 24 announced
topics.quote: first, the citizens party caucus will be held on monday, march 9 at 7:00 pm at the lunenburg middle high school auditorium, which serves as one of two pathways to appear on the ballot for elected boards. second, a public presentation and q&a on the fire department's fourth shift proposal will be held at the lunenburg adult activity center on tuesday, february 24 at 5:00 pm, and will be recorded by pacc for later viewing.

topics.resolution: No public comment received in person or via Zoom

topics.topic: Fire Chief Patrick Sullivan retirement acknowledgment
topics.resolution: Retirement effective November 6, 2026 acknowledged; formal acknowledgment to be scheduled
topics.quote: town manager warren-dyment shared that fire chief patrick sullivan, after 42 years of service, has submitted notification of his intent to retire effective november 6, 2026.

topics.topic: Kimberly Gauvin appointment as Payroll and Benefits Coordinator
topics.resolution: Ratified 4-0
topics.quote: motion by chair nuzzolo to ratify the town manager's appointment of kimberly gauvin as payroll and benefits coordinator. seconded by vice-chair moore. call for vote: four-aye. the motion passed unanimously (4-0-0).

topics.resolution: Preliminary budget nearing completion; shortfall exceeding $3,000,000 noted; will be presented to Finance Committee February 19
topics.quote: the preliminary fy27 budget is nearing completion and will be presented to the finance committee on thursday, february 19. the town manager cautioned that the budget will not be balanced and will be reliant on an override, with the current projected shortfall exceeding $3,000,000.

topics.resolution: Close-out progressing well; preliminary free cash estimated over $3,000,000; Town Manager to consider contributions to Stabilization Fund
topics.quote: the town manager reported that fy25 close-out is progressing well, with an extension through the end of february. revenue and expenditure budgets are balanced, and cash reconciliation is nearly complete. preliminary free cash is estimated at over $3,000,000, attributable in part to a significant school turn-back and strong investment income.

topics.resolution: Food Pantry concerned about timeline; PACC making progress on relocation
topics.quote: the town manager reported that the food pantry expressed concern about a timeline misunderstanding, they had interpreted the wind-down timeline in calendar year terms rather than fiscal year terms, making the prospect of relocating before the next heating season a substantial challenge.

topics.resolution: Administrative Board transferred funds to stabilization and capital account rather than returning to member communities
topics.quote: the meeting addressed the disposition of $433,000 in free cash generated by the district. the administrative board declined to return the funds to member communities, opting instead to retain a portion in free cash and transfer the balance to the district's stabilization and capital account, given anticipated assessment increases as grants supporting newer members hudson and sterling expire.

topics.resolution: Open positions announced; Cable Advisory Committee formation announced
topics.quote: open positions include staff librarian (young adult department), outreach coordinator, recreation director, special assistant to the assessors, and dietary aide. the town manager also announced the formation of the cable advisory committee, with a public announcement forthcoming later in the week.

topics.resolution: Approved 4-0
topics.quote: motion by chair nuzzolo to declare the electric range stove from the lunenburg adult activity center as surplus property. seconded by vice-chair moore. call for vote: four-aye. the motion passed unanimously (4-0-0).

topics.topic: FY26 goals and objectives mid-year review
topics.resolution: Goals reviewed; several objectives modified; progress affirmed
topics.quote: the select board conducted a mid-year review of the fy26 select board and town manager goals and objectives

topics.topic: Notice of Town Meeting warrant article
topics.resolution: Revised language approved specifying notification details and opt-in physical copy provision
topics.quote: the following language revisions were agreed upon: (1) a new sentence specifying that the notification shall include sufficient information to reasonably direct residents to the full text of the warrant; and (2) a sentence affirming that the select board's office shall maintain an opt-in list of residents who wish to receive a physical copy of the warrant mailed to their household at least 14 days prior to town meeting.

topics.resolution: Articles noted as straightforward; presentation at Town Meeting anticipated
topics.quote: two articles were noted, a multi-year allocation of $15,000 and a gift account article, both described as straightforward.

topics.resolution: Two articles characterized as standard housekeeping for Enterprise Fund
topics.quote: town manager warren-dyment characterized two annual pacc articles as standard housekeeping related to the enterprise fund, one restoring $31,271.94 to the town general fund and one appropriating $209,000 from expected income for operations.

topics.resolution: Two articles noted; bylaws amendment and legal research appropriation; Commission invited to present
topics.quote: two articles were noted. the first would amend the bylaws to allow the select board to disperse trust fund commission funds in the absence of a quorum; the select board acknowledged this is a significant change requiring further deliberation, and the trust fund commission has been invited to present at the next select board meeting.

topics.resolution: Proposal to formalize as standing committee; chair invited to present
topics.quote: the select board discussed a proposal to formalize the open space committee as a standing committee via bylaw, replacing its current status as an ad hoc advisory body under the planning board.

topics.resolution: Approved with revision; formal vote deferred to March 3
topics.quote: a formal vote was deferred to the march 3 meeting to allow the full select board to be present, as the chair will be absent and member brian lehtinen was not in attendance.

topics.topic: Legislative earmarks for FY27 state budget
topics.resolution: Status discussed; no formal action; deadline end of March
topics.quote: the select board briefly discussed the status of potential earmark requests. chair nuzzolo noted that the adult activity center ramp does not yet have a cost estimate, which may affect whether it is included.

topics.resolution: Reports from library, MPO, Master Plan, Stormwater, Finance, Capital Planning, and Bylaw Review committees
topics.quote: member glenn mcleod reported upcoming attendance at the library board of trustees on thursday and the mpo the following day, and noted that the master plan steering committee is in its final editing phase.

topics.topic: Public comment at end of meeting
topics.resolution: John Bowen addressed board on tax rate alternative
topics.quote: john bowen, 162 highland street, addressed the select board. mr. bowen recalled a recommendation he made approximately two years ago suggesting that rather than pursuing overrides, the town consider increasing the tax rate by approximately $1.66 per thousand, which he estimated would generate $5,000,000 annually into the town's coffers.

topics.resolution: Meeting adjourned at 8:31 PM
topics.quote: motion by clerk emkey to adjourn at 8:31 pm. seconded by vice-chair moore. call for vote: four-aye. the motion passed (4-0-0).
